business_problem: Rapid growth in digital banking, mobile payments, online wealth services and inclusive finance increased transaction and compute demand. Changsha Bank also needed to operate heterogeneous AI compute efficiently, manage models of different sizes, and scale AI into financial workflows while modernizing its core systems and cloud-native architecture.
solution_summary: Changsha Bank worked with Huawei on a cloud-native, distributed technology foundation for its banking workloads. Huawei Cloud Stack provides a full-stack, multi-cloud platform designed for mixed processor architectures; Kunpeng servers host the migrated online-banking and network-connect core systems. For AI, the bank combines Huawei's hybrid-cloud platform with an Ascend AI computing base and a five-part system for compute, models, knowledge, R&D and evaluation. This addresses heterogeneous compute scheduling and management of small and large models, supporting AI across more than 40 financial scenarios. Reported deployments include credit, risk-control and wealth-marketing use cases, plus the Le series AI assistants for wealth questions, recommendations and planning, and intelligent credit-report generation. The page reports compute-utilization and inference gains but does not detail data ingestion or storage design.

business_outcome: The bank reports AI support for more than 40 financial scenarios, threefold compute utilization, development cycles shortened from months to weeks, twice the inference performance, improved wealth-service efficiency and customer-profile accuracy, and greater than 80% accuracy for the reported credit debit-deduction task.
